sources.density_kg_m3: close to the mineral density of quartz; rounded to 10 kg/m³; initial value, tuned in P1-07
sources.erodibility: judgment, relative to granite: recrystallised quartz, among the most resistant rocks; bedrock ranked by rock strength: river incision scales roughly with tensile strength^-2 (Sklar & Dietrich 2001, Geology 29(12):1087–1090) and lithologic K contrasts span orders of magnitude (Stock & Montgomery 1999, JGR 104(B3):4983–4993); the strength-based contrast is compressed to its square root, so bedrock spans about 0.3–4; initial value, tuned in P1-07
sources.diffusivity: judgment, relative to granite: barely weathers chemically; thin, sandy soils; hillslope transport coefficient D of Roering, Kirchner & Dietrich 1999 (WRR 35(3):853–870), used as a linear creep multiplier and scaled by how readily the rock makes mobile soil (soil production function, Heimsath et al. 1997, Nature 388:358–361): loose and friable classes 2–5, soft sedimentary 1.2–2, crystalline 0.5–1; initial value, tuned in P1-07
sources.vanilla_fallback: last fallback entry (MIC rock-tag README, Fallbacks table)

notes: Quartzite: metamorphosed quartz sandstone, among the hardest rocks at the surface.
